answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on an attestation graph: starting from trusted seeds, each node receives weight equal to the walk’s arrival probability. A Sybil cluster separated by a sparse external cut has low conductance Φ, so its probability mass can escape by at most roughly tΦ over t steps; min-cut transitivity therefore bounds its aggregate voting weight regardless of identity count. Independent seed labels—opal, umber, and lagoon—further limit correlated capture.
